exposure: Timing of hospital admission (immediate vs. delayed) for stillbirth delivery following late intrauterine fetal death (IUFD)
Gestational age at IUFD (early vs. late)
outcome: Maternal laboratory parameters (hemoglobin, thrombocytes, CRP, leucocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes)
cohort: Women who suffered a singleton IUFD ≥ 21 gestational weeks and delivered the stillborn at a tertiary referral center between 2003 and 2019
finding: The study found no clinical superiority of immediate hospital admission for stillbirth delivery compared to delayed admission under stable medical circumstances.
mod_finding: No significant difference regarding delivery mode, labor duration, use of intrapartum analgesia, need for episiotomy and risk of perineal injury was observed between immediate and delayed admission groups.
